title: Cai & Ugai slope, pile row D1/D = 3

meta.title: Cai & Ugai slope, pile row D1/D = 3

source.derived_from: cSlope verification problem V013c (MIT License), https://github.com/ZilanCiftci/cslope
notes: The Ito & Matsui force acts at the resultant of the soil pressure on the pile above the slip surface (about 1.2 m above the crossing here), the moment of the pressure acting from the pile head down: 1.437. At the slip surface, as Cai & Ugai (2000, eq. 9) apply it, it has the longest arm and gives 1.450 (+1.4 %); program D 1.451. Commercial program A directs the force along the slip surface by default and gives 1.432 in cSlope with that direction. Cai & Ugai 1.37 (printed in their table 3, simplex search; docs/kallor/cai-ugai-2000.md). With the force at the slip surface cSlope gives 1.450 (V013c), 1.342 (V013d) and 1.260 (V013e), further from both the programs and the paper than the resultant location, which is kept.
cSlope fija options.tolerance = 0.001 (tolerancia del solver) en sus checks; no se importa: ogs usa analysis.tolerance = 1e-05.
